film.title: Where Art Thou, Julio? The Day the .516 Hitter Vanished in the Bronx
film.description:
Saturday, April 20, 1985. Yankee Stadium. Cleveland's shortstop is hitting .516, best in the American League, and he never shows up.

Julio Franco's manager tore up the lineup card. The team called the police, the hospitals and his wife. Hours later a childhood friend called: Julio was sick at a house in New York with no telephone. He was fined a day's pay. Then he spent the next 30 years refusing to leave baseball: a batting title, an All-Star MVP, a home run at 48, a big-league hit at 49, and pro ball at 55 and 56.

A JuiceBall film from JuiceboxNation.com, with Hardwood Bricks and 19 North Films. Written and narrated by Matthew Hagan, whose first season in memory was the 1985 Tribe. Matthew appears in part as an AI avatar made with HeyGen. Carmine Bellini is a fictional AI anchor and is not affiliated with Fordham University. Music is original.

Sources: SABR Games Project, "April 20, 1985: Where art thou, Julio Franco?" (Andrew Harner); SABR BioProject; Baseball-Reference; Sports Illustrated (Apr. 29, 1985; Feb. 2005); MLB.com; ESPN; AP; UPI; Akron Beacon Journal and Cleveland Plain Dealer via SABR; NBA.com; New York Giants; Guinness World Records. Sept. 17, 2007 footage: MLB, used briefly for commentary.

reels.title: Hitting .516. Gone.
reels.text: April 20, 1985. Cleveland's shortstop is leading the American League at .516, and nobody can find him. Carmine Bellini of the Bronx Sentinel takes the case.

reels.title: The man baseball couldn't get rid of
reels.text: Julio Franco went missing for one afternoon in 1985. Then he homered at 48, got a big-league hit at 49 and was still playing pro ball at 56.
